title: Serving Runtime — Candidate synthesis and onboarding plan (Apr 7–9, 2025)
content:
Meeting context and purpose:
This is a synthesis of the hiring syncs held across Apr 7–9, 2025 for the Serving Runtime hiring slots. Focus: close 2 IC3–IC4 backend engineer openings with emphasis on inference throughput, kernel debugging, and production hardening experience. We also align on onboarding capacity, mentor assignments, and a short ramp curriculum.

Attendees:
- Aisha Patel (owner)
- Ethan Miller
- Priya Shah
- Diego Alvarez
- Maya Chen
- (intermittent): Rahul Iyer (SRE interview shadow)

Agenda:
1) Quick candidate debriefs (3 rounds from last week)
2) Hiring rubric tweaks (latency debugging vs architecture tradeoffs)
3) Onboarding slots & buddy assignments for May onboarding wave
4) Risks to team health and mitigations
5) Action items and owners

Candidate debriefs (summary):
- Candidate A — Backend inference engineer (strong systems debugging)
  - Interview highlights: excellent profiling examples (how they found a KV cache thrash), concrete kernel-level optimization story, fast at reproducing perf regressions locally.
  - Weaknesses: lighter on distributed autoscaling experience and limited exposure to GPU memory fragmentation strategies.
  - Recommendation: hire as IC3 with expectation to pair with Diego on GPU memory experiments.

- Candidate B — Generalist backend (broad but shallow)
  - Interview highlights: solid product sense and team fit; good on system design but no deep LLM-serving experience.
  - Weaknesses: no prior work debugging attention implementation or quantization implications.
  - Recommendation: strong culture add, consider for IC2.5/IC3 with training plan focused on serving-specific tooling.

- Candidate C — Senior infra (distributed systems focus)
  - Interview highlights: designed autoscaling policy for a request-heavy service at previous company, brought real-world SLO tradeoffs and fallback strategies.
  - Weaknesses: not hands-on with model kernels, prefers orchestration and policy-level work.
  - Recommendation: hire as IC4 if pipeline includes a technical upskilling plan for kernel debugging; good match for routing/smart-routing work.

Hiring rubric adjustments proposed:
- Add explicit scoring for: kernel-level debugging (0–4), KV/prefix cache patterns (0–4), and quantization/precision tradeoffs (0–3).
- Reduce weight on pure breadth product-governance questions; increase weight on measurable perf case study (ask candidates to walk through a real perf regression they fixed and metrics used).
- Insert a short take-home profiling exercise for final onsite loop (2–3 hours) with synthetic model and a small perf bug to root cause.

Onboarding & ramp plan (May cohort):
- Capacity: two onboarding buddies (Ethan, Priya) will each take 1 new hire; Maya will be second-buddy for infra-related topics.
- Week 0 (pre-onboard): repo access, local dev guide, perf benchmarking quickstart doc (owner: Aisha, due Apr 25).
- Week 1: "Served model walkthrough" — live session with runtime maintainers, focus on request lifecycle, caching, KV store. (owner: Diego).
- Week 2: paired debugging rotation — new hire pairs with buddy on a small perf task from backlog (owner: Ethan).
- Month 1 milestone: reproduce a perf regression end-to-end and propose mitigation (assessed by buddy + two reviewers).

Team health observations and risks:
- Onboarding bandwidth squeeze: multiple hires expected across infra org in May; current maintainer bandwidth is limited because of release work (SRV-482). Risk: new hires may be under-mentored if we don't pause non-critical changes.
- Mentorship fatigue: Priya flagged potential burnout risk if mentors take >25% of sprint capacity for two full weeks.
- Interview loop throughput: scheduling delays are adding friction and candidate drop-off (~18% decline rate last month).
- Knowledge gaps: kernel-level training materials are sparse; recruits are increasingly expected to be practical at the kernel/quantization layer.

Mitigations agreed:
- Protect two 0.5 FTE mentor slots per sprint for May onboarding (manager action: Priya to align with eng manager pool).
- Move at-risk release tasks to "post-onboard" backlog where feasible — target to free ~10% capacity.
- Prep a 90-minute kernel crash-course (slides + recorded demo) hosted Apr 30 (owner: Diego + Rahul).
- Shorten interview-to-offer SLA: target 7–10 calendar days from final loop to offer; recruiting to prioritize scheduling blocks.

Action items (owner / due):
- Finalize updated hiring rubric doc and add take-home exercise (owner: Aisha) — due Apr 15, create PR to Confluence.
- Create perf benchmarking quickstart (owner: Aisha) — due Apr 25.
- Schedule kernel crash-course + record (owners: Diego, Rahul) — session Apr 30, record uploaded by May 2.
- Align mentor capacity with eng manager (owner: Priya) — confirm by Apr 18.
- Draft onboarding-week checklist for buddies (owner: Ethan) — due Apr 20.
- Recruiter follow-up: compress scheduling pipeline and block two interview days/week for Serving Runtime (owner: Maya) — confirm blocks by Apr 14.

Loose notes / unresolved questions:
- Should we prioritize hires with direct GPU/kernel experience vs. distributed-systems strength? (tradeoff: immediate perf-debug wins vs. longer-term architecture).
- How to measure mentor load objectively? (proposal: track hours spent in "onboarding" label in time-tracking, discussed as SRV-503).
- Consider a 2-week "in-team shadow" for hires before assigning on-call responsibilities.

Appendix: candidate scorecards link and quick references:
- Candidate scorecards (internal link): Confluence /display/SRV/Candidate+Scorecards (placeholder)
- Perf regression example to use in take-home: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/examples/regression-007

Notes: keep this doc as the single source for decisions this round. If reviewers agree, I'll push the rubric PR and coordinate with recruiting on compressed timelines.

-- Aisha
summary: Debrief for three recent candidates for serving-runtime roles. Recommendations to hire Candidate A (IC3) and consider Candidate C for IC4 with upskilling. Action items: update rubric, prepare onboarding materials, protect mentor capacity, schedule kernel crash-course. Targets set for mid-April to late-April deliverables.
